On Thu, Aug 31, 2017 at 1:20 AM, 彭丹晓 <pdxia...@126.com> wrote:
Thanks Nick for your kind advice!
My tree was generated by treePL with more than 100 calibrations, and it wasn't the "very short" tree, only with a node diverging to two 0-length branch tips. I think it might caused by too close relationship between the two tip taxa, or lacked variations given their sequences in DNA matrix.
Today I tried to rerun BSM with the tree pruned one of the two 0-length sister branches, and then worked (⊙o⊙). Thus the problem surely happens at that node! Right?
Afterwards I'm going to add more sequences of the two taxa to alignment matrix to gain more variations, if available.
What would you think about it?
Thank you so much!
Best wishes~

Peng Danxiao
2017.8.30

At 2017-08-30 09:50:41, "Nick Matzke" <mat...@nimbios.org> wrote:
Hi Peng,

If you had a 0-length branch in the first place, you probably have other problems in your tree as well -- good dating analyses rarely/never produce such branches.  Or, possibly, your fix of lengthening the branch was not saved to the correct place. 

First, make sure your tree file is actually a valid, well-dated phylogeny, some advice is here:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears-mistakes-to-avoid#fix_short_trees

Then, run the whole analysis over, starting from the beginning (ML analysis), then try BSM.  If none of that works, try increasing the default from 40000 tries to something much higher.

Cheers!
Nick
